title: Birth in Nacogdoches, move to Taft, and being named Ernie Lawrence Fields
summary: Fields gives his birth date, parents, his father's death in 1906, and how he went by Sonny Boy until he named himself.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was born in Nacogdoches, Texas, Sunday at midnight, August 28, 1904. Reverend Thomas Jefferson Fields was my father and Mary Jane Garrett Fields, mother. The baby of the family of three boys and two girls. The family moved to an all black town, Taft, Oklahoma, 1905. At that time, indian territory.
My father was killed accidentally in 1906. I was known as Sonny Boy before school age and until the fifth grade while going to school.
After sixth grade I finally decided I had to have a name, and all of them kidding me--the youngsters--that my people didn't
think enough of me to name me. I always said, well, they wanted me to be sure that I was satisfied with it.

Then, it came out in the Muskogee daily paper, no more Sonny Boy Fields, it's now Ernie Lawrence Fields. I was a very popular kid, but both the boys and girls used to kid me-- I already said that, but they can edit that-- about not having any name, my parents not naming me. My answer was always they wanted to be sure that I had a name that I would be satisfied with. They demanded that I have the honor of naming myself.
